headline: Historic win: South Africa reach World Cup knockouts for first time
summary: A 1-0 victory over South Korea secures a spot in the knockout stage, ending a decades-long drought for the South African team.
details: South Africa has reached the knockout phase of a World Cup for the first time in its history after defeating South Korea 1-0 on Wednesday.
Thapelo Maseko scored the decisive goal in the 63rd minute, firing the ball into the bottom corner to secure the win.
The victory puts South Africa on four points, placing them behind Group A winners Mexico in the standings.
South Africa will now face co-hosts Canada in Los Angeles on June 28 as they continue their historic run.
This achievement marks a major breakthrough for the team, which had previously failed to advance from the group stage in 1998, 2002, and 2010.
caption:
History made! South Africa has reached the World Cup knockout stage for the first time ever.

South Africa has reached the knockout phase of a World Cup for the first time in its history after defeating South Korea 1-0 on Wednesday.

Thapelo Maseko scored the decisive goal in the 63rd minute, firing the ball into the bottom corner to secure the win.

The victory puts South Africa on four points, placing them behind Group A winners Mexico in the standings.

South Africa will now face co-hosts Canada in Los Angeles on June 28 as they continue their historic run.

This achievement marks a major breakthrough for the team, which had previously failed to advance from the group stage in 1998, 2002, and 2010.

headline_marked: 7.2-magnitude quake hits Japan: [[no major damage or casualties]] reported
headline: 7.2-magnitude quake hits Japan: no major damage or casualties reported
summary: A powerful earthquake struck off the coast of northern Japan on Thursday, causing tremors felt as far as Tokyo, but no tsunami warning was issued.
details: A strong 7.2-magnitude earthquake struck off the coast of northern Japan on Thursday morning. The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) initially reported the magnitude as 6.9 before revising it to 7.2, with the epicenter located at a depth of 44 kilometers.

Tremors were felt several hundred miles away in Tokyo. In Aomori prefecture, the tremors registered an upper six on Japan's seven-level Shindo intensity scale, meaning people may have been thrown off their feet and unsecured furniture toppled.

Despite the intensity, government spokesman Minoru Kihara confirmed there were no reported human casualties. No abnormalities were reported at nuclear power stations in the region, and no tsunami warning was issued.

Minor damage was reported, including overturned tanker trucks, stuck elevators, and some collapsed ceilings in offices. Some shinkansen bullet train services were suspended and a primary school in Hashikami was temporarily closed.
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has ordered government agencies to work closely with local authorities and urged residents in affected areas to remain alert for potential aftershocks.

Japan is one of the world's most seismically active countries, sitting on the 'Ring of Fire'. The nation typically experiences hundreds of jolts annually, accounting for approximately 18 percent of the world's earthquakes.
